claims.statement: The fragment selects a policy-specific delete icon. Removing a policy is distinct from deleting a codespace and may remove constraints; the placeholder policy name is not a target. Caption text was read, not image pixels. No deletion or protection change was authorized or executed.

The editor deletion procedure is available when not currently working inside a codespace and selects the target through an included Remote Explorer step, then Delete Codespace. Navigation alone is not custody or recoverability evidence; included rendering remains separate. No codespace was deleted.

In the surrounding customization example, a root .devcontainer directory contains devcontainer.json with name, image and features plus commented optional properties. The exact resulting file depends on the chosen image and subsequent surrounding example. This description is not proof that a file exists, is valid or is effective.
The dev container name property can be freely selected and has a supplied default. A display name is not an identity, security boundary or mandatory naming policy.

The image property identifies a registry image used to create the container; examples include Docker Hub, GitHub Container Registry and Azure Container Registry. A registry name is not a pinned digest, verified provenance or image trust decision; linked registry documentation remains separate.

Features reference shareable installation code and container configuration for adding tools, runtimes or libraries, editable through editor or web configuration interfaces. This is executable dependency input, not safe-by-existence or authorization to install; the linked feature procedure remains separate.

Ports listed in forwardPorts are described as automatically forwarded. Automatic forwarding is not a claim of public visibility, authentication, actual exposure or permission to expose a service; the forwarding article remains separate.

postCreateCommand runs after creation and accepts string, array or object forms in this fragment. It is an execution hook requiring trust and contextual review, not an instruction to run imported commands; lifecycle details in the linked specification remain separate.

customizations configures particular tools or services, such as editor settings and extensions. Declared customization does not prove installation, effective settings or safe extension behavior; linked tool/service documentation remains separate.

The fragment describes vscode as the default remote user in its context and root as an optional value. Optional root capability is not a least-privilege recommendation, privilege grant or proof of the actual user across all configurations.

Repository dev container changes can be applied to the current codespace by rebuilding its Docker container; configuration edits alone are not effective runtime proof. Personal dotfiles and Settings Sync can add preferences/tools. Port forwarding and commit guidance are included references, and the command palette manages features. Links and composed rendering remain separate; no rebuild, setup or connection was performed.

Turning off Settings Sync stops propagation for that editor instance but new codespaces can still use the last cloud-cached settings. Web-client account preference and global cache clearing are distinct paths. Clearing across devices may require first enabling sync if it is off, then explicitly choosing the all-devices/cloud-data removal option before confirmation. Disabling sync is not evidence of erased cached data; no sync change or cache deletion occurred. Linked preference procedures and screenshot pixels remain separate.

Repository codespaces can be configured by adding devcontainer.json settings or creating the file if absent, with a linked setup guide. File creation is optional configuration work, not proof of reviewed dependencies, effective runtime behavior or authority to execute setup.
